purpose: A natural experiment sitting unused in ICPRB's own table: every WMA water supplier is flat or declining except the one whose service area holds the world's largest data-center concentration.
source: ICPRB 2025 WMA Water Supply Study, Table 4-1 (long-term trend in daily production)
corroboration_note: ICPRB records that Loudoun's employee unit use 'includes industrial, e.g., data centers', with a separate 'Reclaimed Data Centers' line reflecting potable use. The data-center signal is visible in the employee unit-use series.
caveat: Prince William's own employee unit use FELL from 46.4 gpd (2014) to 36.9 (2023) while its data-center stock grew -- consistent with on-site use being small relative to commercial employment, which is this paper's Scope 1 finding. So the Loudoun signal reflects Loudoun's much larger and more water-cooled fleet, not a universal law. State it as suggestive, not causal.
statement: Every WMA supplier is flat or declining except Loudoun Water, at +2.27%/yr -- the one serving the world's largest data-center concentration. Neither ICPRB nor this project has used it. Worth a figure.
